point_one.role: Mechanistic interpretation of the most distinctive biological pattern: the therapy produced a deep but apparently temporary, multi-compartment B-cell reset rather than permanent B-cell elimination.
point_one.new_listener_takeaway: B cells fell sharply in peripheral blood, bone marrow, and cerebrospinal fluid, then began to reappear at a median of about two months. This makes immune reconstitution—and whether clinical signals persist after B-cell return—a central question for the treatment’s future.
point_one.evidence_anchor: FACT-004 supports in-body generation of CD19 CAR-T cells, while FACT-006 reports deep B-cell depletion across three compartments followed by median reappearance after about two months.
point_one.why_it_matters: The result provides a biological rationale for testing one treatment across diseases involving both systemic and central-nervous-system immune activity, but it also shifts the key question from whether B cells can be removed to how durable the resulting clinical changes are.
point_one.must_not_overlap_with_full_story: Do not repeat the basic headline that a single intravenous vector dose generated CD19 CAR-T cells in the body, or simply restate that B cells decreased; focus on the reach across compartments and the timing of their return.
point_one.must_not_overlap_with_other_point: Do not assess the study’s control-group problem, the comparability of disease-specific endpoints, or the strength of the efficacy claim; those are Point Two’s focus.

point_two.role: Interpretive counterweight showing that the reported benefits form a set of disease-specific signals, not one uniform efficacy result that can be pooled across all 16 participants.
point_two.new_listener_takeaway: The outcomes were measured differently across the four diseases: functional and cerebrospinal-fluid changes in progressive MS, fatigue and function changes with antibody decline in only two of three MOG patients, a score reduction in myasthenia gravis, and mainly muscle-biomarker reductions in myositis. The study therefore maps several promising signals rather than demonstrating the same clinical benefit across four conditions.
point_two.evidence_anchor: FACT-007 through FACT-011 provide the disease-specific clinical, antibody, score, imaging, and laboratory findings; FACT-015 establishes that the study was a small, uncontrolled phase 1 trial requiring larger validation.
point_two.why_it_matters: This distinction prevents a biomarker change in one disease from being treated as equivalent to functional improvement in another, and shows why controlled, disease-specific follow-up is needed to determine which signals represent a treatment effect rather than variation that cannot be separated in this design.
point_two.must_not_overlap_with_full_story: Do not re-narrate the overall study, treatment delivery, or each result as a generic success; use the reported findings specifically to contrast the kinds of endpoints and the limits of combining them.
point_two.must_not_overlap_with_other_point: Do not discuss the depth, anatomical distribution, or timing of B-cell depletion and reappearance, or frame the issue around possible retreatment; those belong to Point One.
